specifications.title: Stage Upload For Model Import
specifications.specification: Uploaded File Is Staged Before Business Command Submission
specifications.rule: A file field in a generated form first stages the selected browser file through the FileUpload deployment. The upload adapter stores the file in server-side temporary storage, computes optional checksum metadata, assigns a stagedFileLocation, and returns a stagedFileId to the form. Business commands submit the stagedFileId as a reference and consuming adapters query FileUpload metadata or content before importing the file into durable business storage.

specifications.title: Mark File Consumed By Model Import
specifications.specification: Consumed Staged File Is No Longer User Discardable
specifications.rule: A staged file is marked consumed when a business adapter has imported it into durable business storage, such as a model registry. After consumption, users cannot discard the staged file because the business command has already relied on it. Physical cleanup of the temporary object is handled by retention policy.

specifications.title: Discard Unconsumed Staged File
specifications.specification: Only Unconsumed Staged Files Can Be Discarded
specifications.rule: A user can discard a staged file while it has not been consumed by a business command. Discarding records the intent to remove the temporary file and prevents later business commands from using that staged location.

specifications.title: Reject Discard After Consumption
specifications.specification: Only Unconsumed Staged Files Can Be Discarded
specifications.rule: A user can discard a staged file while it has not been consumed by a business command. Discarding records the intent to remove the temporary file and prevents later business commands from using that staged location.

specifications.title: Register Pullable Model Artifact
specifications.specification: Model Artifact Must Be Pullable And Verifiable
specifications.rule:
Registering a model artifact is a port-backed import operation. modelName identifies the logical model and modelVersion identifies the business version under that model; the pair must be unique. modelId remains the system identity for one immutable imported or trained artifact version. For uploaded files, stagedFileId references a file previously staged by FileUpload, not a browser-local file path. The adapter queries FileUpload metadata or content, imports the staged source model into the managed model registry, marks the staged file consumed after a successful import, detects or validates the model format, computes the artifact digest and size, optionally records a signature URI, and emits a pullable immutable artifact snapshot. modelArtifactUri identifies the concrete pullable artifact for that version.

specifications.title: Select Participants When Runtime Pool Reaches Quorum
specifications.specification: Training Round Participants Are Snapshotted Per Round
specifications.rule: Each training round starts from a runtime snapshot selected by domain policy. The policy evaluates submitted job, locked training configuration, active federation membership, active runtime identity, detected runtime capabilities, connected runtime status, and approved dataset evidence matching the feature schema. Runtimes that become ready after a round has begun cannot join that round, but they can be selected for a later round when policy allows dynamic round snapshots. If the selected runtime count is below quorum, the system records a failed participant selection event so the operator can fix runtime or dataset readiness and retry selection.

The same dataset may be bound on different runtimes, and the same runtime may bind different datasets, but one runtime cannot configure multiple current bindings for the same dataset. Reconfiguration should use an explicit reconfigure/update flow instead of creating another binding for the same runtimeId and datasetId.

specifications.title: Execution Plan Accepted
specifications.specification: Execution Plan Local Acceptance Outcome
specifications.rule: When a participant execution plan is received, the runtime agent performs a local readiness check before starting any training work. The check verifies that the plan targets this runtime, the required dataset binding exists, dataset access has already been validated, the base model is available, the requested training configuration is supported, sufficient local resources are available, and the runtime agent is idle. The port records exactly one outcome: ExecutionPlanAccepted when all local requirements are satisfied, or ExecutionPlanRejected with rejection reasons when any requirement fails.

specifications.title: Round Execution Started
specifications.specification: Round Execution Runtime Engine Start Outcome
specifications.rule: Starting a round execution is responsible for launching the local runtime engine on demand for this participant round, not for calling a pre-existing always-on engine. The adapter prepares the local training workspace and configuration, starts the matching runtime engine service, process, or container, submits the local model training job to that engine, and records the created runtimeEngineJobId. The port records exactly one outcome: RoundExecutionStarted when the runtime engine is running and the training job has been accepted, or RoundExecutionStartFailed when environment preparation, engine startup, model loading, resource allocation, or training job submission fails.

specifications.specification: Runtime Engine Job Observation Outcome
specifications.rule: Observing a runtime engine job is an external status check and must not advance or reset the RoundExecution lifecycle state. The adapter queries the runtime engine by runtimeEngineJobId and records RuntimeEngineJobObserved with observedStatus RUNNING, COMPLETED, or FAILED. Completion and failure domain state changes are triggered by follow-up automations instead of embedding runtime engine polling inside CompleteRoundExecution or FailRoundExecution.

specifications.title: Load Runtime Agent Bootstrap Configuration
specifications.specification: Runtime Agent Startup Bootstrap Configuration
specifications.rule: Runtime agent startup begins by loading bootstrap configuration from environment variables, mounted files, or platform-issued startup material. The configuration must provide the stable runtimeAgentId generated when RuntimeInfrastructure was registered, the matching runtimeInfrastructureId, and the agent version. A successful load starts the runtime-agent lifecycle; a missing or invalid configuration records a bootstrap failure and must not create a new random runtimeAgentId.

specifications.title: Report Runtime Instance Connected
specifications.specification: Runtime Agent Platform Connection Reporting Outcome
specifications.rule: After the runtime instance self-check passes, the runtime agent reports its connection status to the platform by calling POST /runtimeinfrastructure/recordruntimeconnectionestablished. The platform records RuntimeConnectionEstablished only after that command succeeds. The local agent must record AgentRuntimeConnectionReportFailed when the platform API is unreachable, authentication fails, the control channel cannot be established, the heartbeat is rejected, or the platform command is rejected.
